subject: Intro to economic buyer / budget owner — Acme Corp (post-call)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Post-call: Redwood inference intro + next steps

Hi Emily / Jordan,

Thanks again for the time earlier — really appreciate the open discussion about Acme's priorities. Quick recap and suggested next steps: 

- Goals: reduce per-token inference cost for chat/assist workflows, hit p95 latency < 300ms for typical 1k token contexts, and centralize model serving across cloud regions.
- Timeline: internal evaluation through Dec; procurement & approvals targeted early Q1 2027 (you mentioned budget conversations in December).
- Current stakeholders we heard on the call: Emily (Product lead / use-case owner), Jordan (Engineering lead, infra constraints).

Open questions for us (to help tailor next materials):
1) Who is the economic buyer (final approver for budget/contract)?
2) Who owns the budget (procurement/finance contact)?
3) Any specific procurement/legal steps or standard questionnaire we should prepare for?

Attached: post-call-notes.pdf (short bullet summary + initial scoring of decision criteria).

Immediate next step: If you can introduce the economic buyer and budget owner, we'd like to schedule a 30-min sync to: confirm decision criteria, map procurement steps, and walk through our procurement pack (SOC2, data handling, standard terms).

Proposed times (PST): Wed 12/2 10:30am or Thu 12/3 9:00am — happy to adjust.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood inference intro + next steps

Marissa — thanks for the notes and the recap. Helpful.

Quick answers from my side:
- Economic buyer / exec sponsor is likely Samantha Ruiz (VP, Product). She owns the product strategy and signs off on platform spend for product infra.
- Budget owner for procurement is usually Mike Torres (Head of Procurement) — finance will sign off but Mike coordinates contracts and purchase orders.
- Procurement steps: we typically run a short questionnaire, then legal sends redlines (if any). RFP-ish items are sometimes requested for larger deals (> $250k).

I've attached the RFP_requirements.xlsx we sometimes use for infra vendors. Happy to intro Samantha and Mike — looping her in the next reply. If it helps, target we're aiming to have vendor selected by early Jan so timeline looks compatible.

— Jordan

Hi Marissa — welcome, and thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Mike (Head of Procurement) — Mike, please see the notes and Jordan's RFP template.

A few things up front that will help us move quickly:
- Decision criteria: (1) p95 latency and stability under burst (our top priority), (2) predictable unit cost per inference, (3) security & data controls (SOC2 + encryption), (4) migration/rollout support for multiple regions.
- Budget owner: Mike Torres will manage the PO and finalize budget.
- Timeline: we'd like to complete vendor selection by mid-Jan and have contracting started in late Jan / early Feb; so an intro this week is great.

Mike — can you confirm the procurement questionnaire you need? If you prefer, Marissa, feel free to send the standard questionnaire directly to Mike (mike.torres@acme-corp.com). If it helps, attach your SOC2 and a short SOW/pricing range so procurement has context.
